sections.title: Bringing the first half of Unit 29 together
sections.content: szerintem, azt hiszem and gondolom all open an opinion, with slightly different shades of certainty — szerintem is the most neutral and common. inkább says what you'd rather do right now; jobban szeretem compares how much you like two named things. -bb + mint extends to comparing anything you can name (Ez az étterem jobb, mint az.), leg- picks a winner among three or more, and egyformán says two things are simply tied.

sections.title: Opinions and comparisons, recapped
rows: in my opinion / I think, I believe / I guess
I'd rather drink tea than coffee.
Jobban szeretem a teát, mint a kávét.
I like tea better than coffee.
Melyik jobb? A két étterem egyformán jó.
Which is better? The two restaurants are equally good.

items.spanish: Azt hiszem, ez a jobb megoldás.
items.english: I think this is the better solution.
I'd rather walk than take the bus.

items.spanish: Jobban szeretem a magyar konyhát, mint az olaszt.
items.english: I like Hungarian cuisine better than Italian.

items.spanish: Szerintem ez a legszebb város Magyarországon.
items.english: In my opinion, this is the most beautiful city in Hungary.

sections.content: jobban szeretem compares two named things you both like to some degree; inkább is about the choice you're making right now — often you'll reach for both together in the same conversation.
